Tess (support): Heads-up: customer DataFox (CS-4827) reports a big regression on embeddings endpoint starting ~2025-11-05 03:00 UTC. Vectors/sec dropped ~60%, p95 latency up from 120ms -> 650ms, retries spiked. They also sometimes see "dimension mismatch" errors in client logs when batching. They attached a small repro load test.

Liam (eng-ml): Do we have the exact model version they're calling and the batcher config? dimension mismatch could be client-side, but throughput drop + GPU numbers point at runtime.

Tess (support): Model: open-embedder-large-v2@v3 (pinned on their account). Batcher config in their request: they call /v1/embeddings with batch size 8 (client side) repeatedly. I'll paste the minimal repro they gave.

Tess (support): ```bash
# curl repro (customer)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-embedder-large-v2@v3","inputs":["text1","text2",...],"batch_size":8}'
```

Tess (support): Their client sometimes logs: "Expected embedding dimension 1024 but got 1536" — they say this happens ~1% of requests and corresponds to the high-latency tail.

Evan (infra): I pulled infra metrics for their tenant and the global pool during the window. GPU util on node gpu-pool-11 jumped to 93% but SM clocks were lower than normal. Memory usage shows more frequent mem spikes and >1.1k concurrent queued inference requests in the local queue (queue depth). NVML snapshot (trimmed):

Evan (infra): ```
$ nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv
pid, process_name, used_memory
23456,python,18432 MiB
23478,python,16800 MiB
...

# runtime watcher:
GPU Utilization: 93%
GPU Memory Used: 89%
Active Inference Workers: 16
Local Queue Depth: 1203
Average Batch Size (served): 2.1
Vector throughput (vectors/sec): 2,200 -> normally 6,200
Token-based gen throughput irrelevant here but included for comparison: tokens/sec unaffected on gen nodes
```

Liam (eng-ml): Average batch size 2.1 is the smoking gun — system is getting lots of small micro-batches. That kills vector throughput because embedding model does a full forward pass per batch and benefits from larger batch sizes. The intermittent dimension mismatch suggests sometimes a different variant (maybe @v2) is being routed in fallback, or there's a serialization bug in the response envelope. We recently deployed (last night) a routing change that allows falling back to quantized variants when OOM is close — could be returning a 1536-dim quantized model accidentally.

Aria (oncall): @Deploy Bot do we have the deploy that changed routing/fallback behavior?

Deploy Bot: New deployment 2025-11-05T02:45Z: routing/fallback-service v1.7.2 -> v1.8.0 (canary roll: 20% traffic).

Evan (infra): That lines up. v1.8.0 started canarying at 02:45Z; customer started seeing regressions ~03:00Z. Logs show a spike in fallback decisions for large models due to temporary memory pressure. The fallback chosen sometimes points to an incompatible model family (bad mapping) — that would explain dimension mismatch.

Liam (eng-ml): Two things to verify in parallel: 1) confirm fallback mapping bug (does the code ever map open-embedder-large-v2 to a 1536-dim variant?), 2) reproduce throughput regression by running a load generator against staging with the same canary routing. I can run loadgen if Evan gives me a staging snapshot.

Evan (infra): Preparing a staging snapshot (same mem footprint) — expected ETA 25m. In the meantime, can we get customer's raw HTTP traces? Specifically X-Redwood-Model, X-Redwood-Variant headers and latencies.

Tess (support): Asked customer to provide request traces and a small set of failing request IDs. They've shared X-Redwood-Request-Ids for 12 failed calls. I'll drop them in #sec with PII scrubbed.

Liam (eng-ml): Also, check the batcher configuration in the runtime: I want to see continuous batching window and max_batch_size. If the continuous batcher was disabled in v1.8.0 due to a bug, that would explain average batch size falling to ~2.

Evan (infra): I grepped the v1.8.0 diff — there was a change to the batcher preemption logic to favor latency SLOs which unintentionally disabled the batching delay for requests tagged as "interactive". Some customers set interactive via SDK heuristics. Looks like DataFox SDK sets interactive=true for their call pattern. That would make the runtime flush batches immediately, producing many small batches.

Aria (oncall): Action items:
- Liam: reproduce load in staging with v1.8.0 canary routing + same SDK flags (priority: now -> 2h).
- Evan: roll back the routing/fallback canary to 0% for the affected pool (priority: now). If rollback not possible, block the fallback mapping step.
- Tess: keep customer updated and collect request headers/traces.

Liam (eng-ml): Repro plan (short):
1) deploy v1.8.0 canary to staging (same split)
2) run loadgen: 1k concurrent connections, client batch=8, realistic inter-arrival to mimic small bursts (Poisson)
3) measure avg batch size, vectors/sec, p95 latency, GPU util
4) toggle batcher delay to restore normal behavior (e.g., enable continuous batching delay=15ms, max_batch_size=64) and compare

Liam (eng-ml): Quick snippet to run locally against staging:
```
# python loadgen snippet (requests per sec ~1200)
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import requests
URL = 'https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
HEADERS = {'Authorization':'Bearer STAGING', 'Content-Type':'application/json'}
PAYLOAD = {'model':'open-embedder-large-v2@v3', 'inputs':['short text']*8, 'batch_size':8}

def worker(i):
    r = requests.post(URL, json=PAYLOAD, headers=HEADERS, timeout=20)
    return r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-Redwood-Variant')

with ThreadPoolExecutor(200) as ex:
    for _ in range(1200):
        ex.submit(worker, _)
```

Tess (support): Customer replied: they see X-Redwood-Variant rotate between open-embedder-large-v2@v3 and open-embedder-quant-1536@v1 during the error windows. They NEVER requested the quantized variant.

Evan (infra): Confirmed: fallback mapping table had an entry mismatch (index off-by-one) introduced in v1.8.0 crate. When OOM triggers fallback, it sometimes picks look-up index N+1 which is a quantized variant of a different architecture (1536 dims). Patch incoming. Rolling canary back now.

Deploy Bot: Rolling rollback: routing/fallback-service -> v1.7.2 started at 03:22Z. Canary traffic -> 0% by 03:24Z.

Evan (infra): Early telemetry post-rollback (5m window): local queue depth dropped from ~1200 -> 300, average batch size increased to 5.8, vectors/sec recovered to ~5,500 but still slightly below baseline. Dimension-mismatch errors dropped to zero in the sampled trace.

Liam (eng-ml): That matches expectations: two root causes — (A) fallback mapping bug returning wrong-dimension variants and (B) a batching preemption change that reduced batch sizes for interactive-tagged requests. Fix both: patch mapping table (hotfix), and revert the preemption change or add a guard (only apply for models with a known interactive latency profile).

Aria (oncall): Can we propose mitigations for customers in the meantime?

Liam (eng-ml): Mitigations: 1) set SDK flag interactive=false for bulk embedding calls, 2) client-side explicit batching (batch_size >= 16) to increase per-request throughput, 3) we can pin to v1.7.2 routing via account-level override while we verify the patch.

Tess (support): Passing mitigations to DataFox. They asked for a timeline. ETA for hotfix?

Evan (infra): Hotfix for mapping table already staged, QA run now. I expect 30–45m for hotfix rollout + verification. Batcher preemption revert needs a little more review — target in today's patch window (3–4h).

Liam (eng-ml): I'll run the prescribed loadgen against the hotfix and also test enabling continuous batching delay=15ms in staging to quantify improvements.

Tess (support): Customer acknowledged. They will try explicit batching on their end and set interactive=false. They've also asked for a credit for the spike in billing due to retries — flagged to billing.

Aria (oncall): Summarize for postmortem: cause = faulty routing fallback mapping + batcher preemption change. Impact = 60% drop in vector throughput for affected pool, p95 latency increased, transient dimension-mismatch errors, billing spike for affected accounts. Remediation = rollback canary, hotfix mapping table, revert/guard preemption change, tenant pin option. Owner assignments noted.

Tess (support): I'll keep the thread live with customer updates and attach final telemetry once hotfix verified. Closing loop: immediate rollback done; hotfix ETA ~35m; batcher revert ETA today. Will follow up with PM/eng for postmortem draft. :thumbsup:

Liam (eng-ml): Thanks team. I'll ping when I have staged results.

Deploy Bot: Hotfix deploy 2025-11-05T03:40Z scheduled: routing/fallback-service v1.8.1 (fix mapping).

Evan (infra): Hotfix applied at 03:41Z. Post-hotfix sample: vectors/sec -> 6,100, avg batch size -> 6.2, queue depth -> 210. No dimension-mismatch observed in 10k sampled requests.

Tess (support): Sent update to DataFox. They confirmed recovery and will accept billing credit conversation with billing. Closing action: PM to own postmortem and follow-up tasks.

Aria (oncall): Marking incident for postmortem. Thanks all.
